Why Augusta Homes Need Pest Control

Butler County's climate creates a perfect storm for pest activity. The average temperature swings between forty-nine and sixty-nine degrees throughout the year, but it's the thirty-eight freeze-thaw cycles annually that cause real problems. These cycles create microscopic cracks in foundations, expand gaps around utility penetrations, and compromise weather stripping—giving ants, spiders, mice, and other pests dozens of entry points into your home.

The eleven inches of snowfall combined with spring rainfall creates moisture accumulation around foundations, particularly in homes near Garvin Park and Jim Brown Park where mature trees and landscaping can trap water against structures. This moisture attracts termites, carpenter ants, and creates ideal breeding grounds for mosquitoes during warmer months. Living in USDA Plant Hardiness Zone 6b means our moderate winters rarely kill off pest populations completely—they simply move indoors when temperatures drop.

Recent flash flooding events in Butler County have displaced rodent populations and increased cockroach activity as pests seek higher ground. With a median household income of $68,046, most Augusta families have invested significantly in their homes and can't afford the structural damage that goes unnoticed until it's expensive to repair. Regular pest control isn't a luxury here—it's structural maintenance.

Our Pest Control Process In Augusta

Shaw's Pest Control begins every service with a thorough inspection of your property's unique vulnerabilities. We examine foundation lines, check crawl spaces and attics, inspect around utility entry points, and identify the specific pest pressures your home faces. Our technicians hold Three State Certifications and Master Tech Certification, meaning they're trained to identify not just the pests you see, but the conditions that attract them in the first place.

We then create a customized treatment plan based on what we find. Interior treatments target baseboards, entry points, and problem areas using products that are effective against pests but safe for your family and pets. Exterior treatments create a protective barrier around your foundation, under eaves, and around doors and windows—the places where pests attempt entry. We pay special attention to areas where Butler County's weather creates vulnerabilities.

Our service includes follow-up visits to ensure treatments remain effective through changing seasons.
